To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nearest-neighbor induced structural changes observed in a library of GxG peptide fragments are much less pronounced for a coil library and that these structural changes are relevant for a quantitative description of unfolded proteins, but are less important for proteins with residual structure.
(i) nearest-neighbor interactions have a strong influence on the conformation of amino acid residues, and that (ii) the magnitude of these effects depends strongly on the local sequence context.

the statistical coil states, as defined by Ramachandran maps of xy-pairs, of unfolded proteins can be described by the sum of the conformational propensity of individual amino acid residues and nearest-neighbor effects, which are much less pronounced for unfolded than for regular secondary structure segments, as observed in the GxyG peptides, and that these nearest-neighbor interactions can be utilized for a more complete physical description of unfolded proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of nearest-neighbor effects on the conformation of amino acids in the statistical coil state.
the analysis and comparison of the conformational distributions of unfolded and intramolecularly disordered proteins.
the analysis of nearest-neighbor induced structural changes in amino acid residues in proteins and peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the statistical coil state is characterized by the absence of any significant conformational preference, but the conformational space accessible to a given residue in a coil library is not necessarily identical to that in an unfolded protein.
nearest-neighbor induced structural changes in unfolded and intrisically disordered proteins are significant, but that they are not sufficient to explain the observed conformational ensemble.
nearest-neighbor induced structural changes in unfolded proteins are not negligible and can be quantified by means of the above described method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nearest-neighbor interactions are not only relevant for regular secondary structure but also for the coil state of unfolded and intrinsecally disordered proteins.

the conformational propensity of an amino acid residue in the statistical coil state is a function of its local environment and that the local environment is not necessarily limited to the next residue in the primary sequence.

we are able to show that nearest neighbor interactions are important to describe the conformational state of an unfolded protein, but that the extent of these interactions is dependent on the particular protein and its environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conformational propensity of amino acid residues can be significantly affected by their nearest neighbors.
the analysis of Ramachandrn plots of xy-pair libraries is a powerful method to quantify nearest-neighbor effects in peptides and proteins.
nearest-neighbor induced structural changes can be utilized for a more complete physical understanding of the statistical ensemble of amino acid side chains in unfolded proteins.
